methods.label: Sum the horizontal and vertical movements
methods.explanation:
The directions repeat right, up, left, down. Thus the horizontal displacements are \(1,-\frac14,\frac1{16},\ldots\), while the vertical displacements are \(\frac12,-\frac18,\frac1{32},\ldots\). Both are geometric series with common ratio \(-\frac14\). Since its absolute value is less than \(1\), the endpoint coordinates approach
\[
X=\frac{1}{1+\frac14}=\frac45,
\qquad
Y=\frac{\frac12}{1+\frac14}=\frac25.
\]
After \(k\) moves, the remaining total travel is
\[
2^{-k}+2^{-k-1}+\cdots=2^{1-k},
\]
which tends to zero. Therefore the whole path, including positions between endpoints, approaches \((\frac45,\frac25)\) arbitrarily closely.

To compare all the choices, note that moves in either coordinate alternate in direction and shrink by a factor of \(\frac14\). Consequently the bug always has \(y\le\frac12\). The points in A, C, and E therefore remain at least \(\frac16,\frac3{10},\frac3{10}\) unit away, respectively.

For D, the first segment has \(y=0\), and the second has \(x=1\), giving distance at least \(\frac13\) on those segments. From the end of the second move onward, \(x\ge\frac34\): the move left reaches \(\frac34\), and the smaller alternating horizontal moves stay between \(\frac34\) and \(1\). Thus all these later positions are at least
\[
\frac34-\frac23=\frac1{12}
\]
from D. Only B can be approached arbitrarily closely, so the answer is \((\frac45,\frac25)\), choice B.
